stemMd: Which statement must be true in every permitted order?

options.label: A
options.textMd: Accord must not be in position 2.

options.label: C
options.textMd: Code and Deed must not occupy consecutive positions.

explanationMd:
Combine the ordering and placement constraints rather than assuming one example is unique. The statement "Code and Deed must not occupy consecutive positions." holds in all 2 permitted orders. Generate the cases by placing any fixed-position item and adjacent block first, then discard arrangements that violate a remaining rule. For each alternative, an explicit permitted counterexample appears in its feedback.

Complete permitted orders (each arrow advances one position):
- Code → Edict → Accord → Deed → Bill
- Edict → Accord → Deed → Bill → Code

distractorRationale.a: A counterexample satisfying all the rules is Edict → Accord → Deed → Bill → Code. Thus this statement is not necessary.
distractorRationale.b: A counterexample satisfying all the rules is Edict → Accord → Deed → Bill → Code. Thus this statement is not necessary.
distractorRationale.d: A counterexample satisfying all the rules is Code → Edict → Accord → Deed → Bill. Thus this statement is not necessary.

independentSolve.workingNotes: Blind re-solve in the 5 November 2026 AI audit of this expansion (the review packet held no key, explanation or distractor notes; status "verified_key_agreement"; it checked for competing defensible answers and flagged none): Independently enumerated all 120 permutations of Accord, Bill, Code, Deed, Edict. Rules Code must occupy position 1 or position 5. Accord must precede Deed. Bill and Edict must not occupy consecutive positions. Exactly 1 other item must occur between Accord and Bill. leave 2 valid orders: Code>Edict>Accord>Deed>Bill; Edict>Accord>Deed>Bill>Code. Choice true counts: a=1, b=1, c=2, d=1; necessary requires all matches.
